data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: analyze
sections.summary: To examine something carefully and in detail in order to understand or explain it.

senses.definition: to examine something carefully and in detail in order to understand or explain it
examples: The scientists carefully analyzed the water samples taken from the river.

senses.definition: to think about something carefully in order to understand what it means
examples: She analyzed the poem and identified several important themes.

senses.definition: the process of studying something carefully to understand it (noun form: analysis)
examples: The analysis of the results took several weeks to complete.

answers.answer: The research team analyzed the survey results to identify key trends.
She analyzed to revise her notes more carefully the night before the exam.
He analyzed his teacher a question about the part he did not understand.
The students analyzed a new list of vocabulary words every Friday in class.

sections.question: communicate
sections.summary: To share or exchange information, ideas or feelings with another person, either by speaking, writing or in other ways.

senses.definition: to share information, news or ideas with others by speaking, writing or other means
examples: Good managers communicate clearly and listen carefully to their teams.

senses.definition: to express feelings or thoughts so that other people understand them
examples: She found it difficult to communicate her ideas in front of the large group.

answers.answer: She communicates very effectively, which is why she is an excellent team leader.
The teacher communicated the students to open their books to page forty-five.
He communicated a long letter and posted it to the university admissions office.
The students communicated the classroom quietly and sat in their usual seats.

sections.question: consider
sections.summary: To think carefully about something, especially before making a decision; also to regard something in a particular way.

senses.definition: to think carefully about something, especially before making a decision
examples: You should consider all the options carefully before making a final decision.

senses.definition: to regard someone or something in a particular way
examples: Many people consider him to be one of the greatest writers of the twentieth century.

answers.answer: The committee carefully considered each application before making their final choice.
She considered her homework quickly and placed it neatly in her bag before class.
He considered the classroom and chose a seat near the window at the back.
The students considered their lunch in the canteen before afternoon classes began.

sections.question: demonstrate
sections.summary: To show clearly how something works or that something is true; also to take part in a public protest.

senses.definition: to show clearly how something is done or how something works
examples: The instructor demonstrated how to use the equipment before students tried it themselves.

senses.definition: to show clearly that something is true by providing evidence
examples: The results demonstrate that the new teaching method is highly effective.

senses.definition: to take part in a public protest or march to show opposition to or support for something
examples: Thousands of students demonstrated outside the parliament building.

answers.answer: The science teacher demonstrated the experiment step by step before the class repeated it.
She demonstrated the book from the shelf and began reading at her desk.
He demonstrated his teacher after class to ask about the upcoming assignment.
The students demonstrated the exercise six times each until the lesson ended.

sections.question: discuss
sections.summary: To talk or write about a topic in detail, considering different ideas or opinions.

senses.definition: to talk about a topic with someone, especially to share opinions or make a decision
examples: The students discussed the causes of climate change in small groups.

senses.definition: to write about a subject and consider different aspects of it
examples: In this essay, we will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of social media.

answers.answer: The class discussed the novel in pairs before sharing their ideas with everyone.
She discussed about the importance of healthy eating in her presentation.
He discussed a new pen from his bag and started writing the answer on the board.
The teacher discussed the students a list of essay topics to choose from.

sections.question: evaluate
sections.summary: To judge or assess the quality, importance or value of something after thinking carefully about it.

senses.definition: to judge or assess the quality, importance or value of something
examples: The teacher evaluated each student's presentation using a detailed checklist.

senses.definition: to consider information or results carefully in order to form a conclusion
examples: The managers evaluated the new system after six months and decided to keep it.

answers.answer: The school board evaluated the new programme after one year to see if it had been successful.
She evaluated to apply for the scholarship after speaking with her teacher about it.
He evaluated a group project to the teacher at the end of the spring term.
The students evaluated the classroom slowly, looking at the posters on every wall.

sections.question: implement
sections.summary: To put a plan, system or decision into action; to start using something that has been officially decided.

senses.definition: to put a plan, policy or decision into effect
examples: The school plans to implement a new digital attendance system from next term.

senses.definition: a tool or piece of equipment used for a particular purpose
examples: Farming implements such as ploughs and hoes have been used for thousands of years.

answers.answer: The government implemented a new policy to reduce plastic waste in schools.
She implemented her friend about the change to the class timetable after lunch.
He implemented to finish the group project before the end of the month.
The students implemented their pens and notebooks as soon as the test papers arrived.

sections.question: negotiate
sections.summary: To discuss something formally with someone in order to reach an agreement; also to successfully deal with a difficult situation or obstacle.

senses.definition: to discuss something formally with someone in order to reach an agreement
examples: The union negotiated a new contract that included a significant pay increase.

senses.definition: to successfully pass through or deal with a difficult situation or obstacle
examples: The driver carefully negotiated the narrow mountain road in the dark.

answers.answer: The two sides negotiated for several weeks before finally reaching an agreement.
She negotiated the entrance exam successfully and was offered a place at the university.
He negotiated to school by bicycle every morning to avoid the heavy traffic.
The students negotiated the exam questions for a few minutes before choosing which to answer.

sections.question: participate
sections.summary: To take part in or become involved in an activity or event.

senses.definition: to take part in an activity or event
examples: All students are encouraged to participate in at least one extracurricular activity.

senses.definition: to be actively involved in a discussion or group activity
examples: She always participates in class discussions and asks thoughtful questions.

answers.answer: Every member of the class was invited to participate in the end-of-year debate.
She participated the school drama competition and won the prize for best actress.
He participated a very good idea during the meeting that everyone agreed with.
The class participated the new vocabulary by reading it aloud together three times.

sections.question: resolve
sections.summary: To find a solution to a problem or disagreement; also used as a noun to mean firm determination to achieve something.

senses.definition: to find a satisfactory solution to a problem or disagreement
examples: The mediator helped both parties resolve their dispute without going to court.

senses.definition: to make a firm decision to do something
examples: After failing the exam, she resolved to study much harder for the retake.

senses.definition: strong determination to achieve something even when it is difficult
examples: She showed great resolve in completing her degree while working full-time.

answers.answer: The two students resolved their disagreement with the help of the class teacher.
She resolved a new textbook from the school library before the project began.
He resolved the students a worksheet to complete before the next lesson.
The teacher resolved the class into groups and asked them to choose a topic.
